reason: This passage from 2 Samuel 13 recounts the narrative of Amnon's assault on his half-sister Tamar. It contains no direct speech from Yahweh, no divine complaint, and no mention of God's reaction or displeasure. The text focuses entirely on human characters and events—specifically Amnon's crime, Tamar's suffering, David's anger upon hearing of the events, and Absalom's silent hatred of Amnon. While David becomes very angry when he learns of these matters, this is a human reaction, not a divine complaint.
